title: Developer relations and documentation
description: Review what developers and users read to adopt the product: API reference, SDKs, guides, tutorials, changelogs and the community around them.
expertises: Public API reference, SDKs and code samples
questions: Who reads the documentation for this change, and what must they be able to do after reading it?
Is the reference generated from the contract, and do the examples run against the released version?
How will developers learn about breaking changes and deprecations, and with how much notice?

sources.title: Diátaxis, a systematic approach to technical documentation
Write the Docs, Docs as Code

specialists.title: API reference writer
specialists.focus: Check that the reference is generated from the API contract, covers every public operation, error and limit, and matches the released version.
checks: The reference is built from the OpenAPI or schema file in the repository, not written by hand.
Every operation documents authentication, errors, rate limits and at least one request and response example.
Deprecated operations are marked deprecated in the contract and in the reference, with the removal date.

specialists.title: Documentation architect
specialists.focus: Place each new page in the right type: tutorial, how-to guide, reference or explanation, and check that readers can find it from where they start.
checks: Each page serves one documentation type and does not mix a tutorial with reference tables.
The change updates every existing page that described the old behaviour.
Documentation lives in version control and is reviewed with the code change.

specialists.title: SDK and code samples maintainer
specialists.focus: Check that SDKs, snippets and sample apps compile and run against the released API, and that their versions follow the API's compatibility policy.
checks: Code samples are tested in CI against the release candidate.
SDK versions follow semantic versioning and the changelog lists breaking changes first.
Samples contain no real keys or customer data; placeholders are obvious.

specialists.title: Developer advocate
specialists.focus: Plan how developers hear about the change, where they ask questions and how their feedback reaches the product team.
checks: Breaking changes are announced with a migration guide before the deprecation period starts.
Questions from the forum, issues or support are tagged so they reach the owning team.
Time to first successful call is measured for new developers.

evidence: API contract file and the generated reference for the change.
Documentation pull request with the pages added and updated.
Results of the code sample and SDK tests against the release candidate.
Changelog entry, deprecation notice and migration guide when behaviour changes.
challenge: Could a developer who has never seen the product complete the main task using only the documentation?
Which example in the docs would fail if copied today?
Is the breaking change necessary, or can the old behaviour stay available during a deprecation period?
Does the documentation promise a behaviour, limit or service level the product does not guarantee?
decision_criteria: Proceed when the reference is generated from the contract, examples run and the changelog describes the change.
Revise when documentation is missing, contradicts the released behaviour or examples fail.
Block a breaking change to a public API until a migration guide and a deprecation period are published.
Name the documentation measure, such as failed sample runs or search queries without results, and its review date.
